494	def _read_table(path: Path) -> Tuple[List[str], List[List[str]]]:
495	    """Read a CSV table into its header and raw data rows (CSV order)."""
496	    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
497	        reader = csv.reader(fh)
498	        try:
499	            header = next(reader)
500	        except StopIteration:
501	            header = []
502	        rows = [list(row) for row in reader]
503	    return header, rows

506	def _join_key(field: str) -> Any:
507	    """Normalize one ON cell.
508	
509	    Finite decimal text joins by exact decimal value (so ``1`` and ``1.0``
510	    match); everything else joins by raw text. A normalized number never
511	    equals a text key, so mixed numeric/text values never match.
512	    """
513	    try:
514	        value = Decimal(field)
515	    except (InvalidOperation, ValueError):
516	        return field
517	    if not value.is_finite():
518	        return field
519	    return value

522	def _resolve_join_column(
523	    table: Optional[str],
524	    name: str,
525	    left_table: str,
526	    right_table: str,
527	    left_header: Sequence[str],
528	    right_header: Sequence[str],
529	) -> Tuple[int, int]:
530	    """Resolve a (possibly bare) reference to ``(side, column_index)``.
531	
532	    Side 0 is the left/FROM table, side 1 the JOIN table. A bare name present
533	    in both headers is ambiguous (ValueError); a missing column is KeyError.
534	    """
535	    if table is not None and table not in (left_table, right_table):
536	        raise ValueError(f"unknown table qualifier {table!r} for column {name!r}")
537	    in_left = name in left_header
538	    in_right = name in right_header
539	    if table is None:
540	        if in_left and in_right:
541	            raise ValueError(
542	                f"column {name!r} is ambiguous: it exists in both "
543	                f"{left_table!r} and {right_table!r}; qualify it with the "
544	                "table name"
545	            )
546	        if not in_left and not in_right:
547	            raise KeyError(
548	                f"column {name!r} does not exist in either {left_table!r} "
549	                f"or {right_table!r}"
550	            )
551	        if in_left:
552	            return 0, left_header.index(name)
553	        return 1, right_header.index(name)
554	    if table == left_table:
555	        if not in_left:
556	            raise KeyError(
557	                f"column {name!r} does not exist in table {left_table!r}"
558	            )
559	        return 0, left_header.index(name)
560	    if not in_right:
561	        raise KeyError(
562	            f"column {name!r} does not exist in table {right_table!r}"
563	        )
564	    return 1, right_header.index(name)
565	
566	
567	def _resolve_on(
568	    on: JoinOn,
569	    left_table: str,
570	    right_table: str,
571	    left_header: Sequence[str],
572	    right_header: Sequence[str],
573	) -> Tuple[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int]]:
574	    """Resolve the ON equality into one (side, index) pair per table.
575	
576	    The two sides must come from different tables, one each; a same-table
577	    pair (after bare resolution) is a ValueError.
578	    """
579	    first = _resolve_join_column(
580	        on.left.table, on.left.name,
581	        left_table, right_table, left_header, right_header,
582	    )
583	    second = _resolve_join_column(
584	        on.right.table, on.right.name,
585	        left_table, right_table, left_header, right_header,
586	    )
587	    if first[0] == second[0]:
588	        raise ValueError(
589	            "ON must compare one column from each table, not two columns of "
590	            "the same table"
591	        )
592	    if first[0] == 0:
593	        return first, second
594	    return second, first
595	
596	
597	def _join_comparison_vector(
598	    pairs: Sequence[Tuple[Sequence[str], Sequence[str]]],
599	    position: Tuple[int, int],
600	    comp: Comparison,
601	) -> List[bool]:
602	    """Evaluate one WHERE comparison over every joined row.
603	
604	    As with the single-table scan, the column is parsed for every joined row
605	    up front: OR never short-circuits numeric cell validation.
606	    """
607	    side, idx = position
608	    vec = [
609	        pair[side][idx] if idx < len(pair[side]) else "" for pair in pairs
610	    ]
611	    result: List[bool] = [False] * len(vec)
612	    if comp.quoted:
613	        target_text = comp.value_text
614	        for i, field in enumerate(vec):
615	            result[i] = _compare(field, comp.op, target_text)
616	    else:
617	        target = Decimal(comp.value_text)
618	        label = comp.column if comp.table is None else f"{comp.table}.{comp.column}"
619	        for i, field in enumerate(vec):
620	            result[i] = _compare(_decimal(field, label), comp.op, target)
621	    return result
622	
623	
624	def _resolve_where_positions(
625	    node: WhereExpr,
626	    positions: Dict[int, Tuple[int, int]],
627	    left_table: str,
628	    right_table: str,
629	    left_header: Sequence[str],
630	    right_header: Sequence[str],
631	) -> None:
632	    if isinstance(node, Comparison):
633	        positions[id(node)] = _resolve_join_column(
634	            node.table, node.column,
635	            left_table, right_table, left_header, right_header,
636	        )
637	        return
638	    for operand in node.operands:
639	        _resolve_where_positions(
640	            operand, positions,
641	            left_table, right_table, left_header, right_header,
642	        )
643	
644	
645	def _eval_join_where(
646	    node: WhereExpr,
647	    pairs: Sequence[Tuple[Sequence[str], Sequence[str]]],
648	    positions: Dict[int, Tuple[int, int]],
649	) -> List[bool]:
650	    """Vectorized boolean-tree evaluation on the joined rows."""
651	    if isinstance(node, Comparison):
652	        return _join_comparison_vector(pairs, positions[id(node)], node)
653	    vectors = [
654	        _eval_join_where(operand, pairs, positions) for operand in node.operands
655	    ]
656	    return _combine(node.op, vectors)

659	def _run_join(data_dir: str, query: Query) -> Dict[str, Any]:
660	    """Execute the single supported INNER JOIN query end to end."""
661	    left_table = query.table
662	    right_table = query.join_table
663	    # Built-in open raises FileNotFoundError, preserving the required type;
664	    # the left (FROM) table is opened before the right (JOIN) table.
665	    left_path = Path(data_dir) / f"{left_table}.csv"
666	    right_path = Path(data_dir) / f"{right_table}.csv"
667	    left_header, left_rows = _read_table(left_path)
668	    right_header, right_rows = _read_table(right_path)
669	
670	    def resolve(table: Optional[str], name: str) -> Tuple[int, int]:
671	        return _resolve_join_column(
672	            table, name, left_table, right_table, left_header, right_header
673	        )
674	
675	    # ON first: it uniquely defines the cross-table column pair.
676	    left_pos, right_pos = _resolve_on(
677	        query.join_on, left_table, right_table, left_header, right_header
678	    )
679	
680	    # Hash the right table by normalized join key; appending in CSV order
681	    # keeps each bucket in right-table CSV order.
682	    right_buckets: Dict[Any, List[Sequence[str]]] = {}
683	    right_idx = right_pos[1]
684	    for row in right_rows:
685	        field = row[right_idx] if right_idx < len(row) else ""
686	        right_buckets.setdefault(_join_key(field), []).append(row)
687	
688	    # SELECT projection positions, resolved up front so unknown/ambiguous
689	    # columns fail before any row is emitted.
690	    select_positions = [
691	        resolve(item.table, item.column) for item in query.select
692	    ]
693	
694	    where_positions: Dict[int, Tuple[int, int]] = {}
695	    if query.where is not None:
696	        _resolve_where_positions(
697	            query.where, where_positions,
698	            left_table, right_table, left_header, right_header,
699	        )
700	
701	    pairs: List[Tuple[Sequence[str], Sequence[str]]] = []
702	    left_idx = left_pos[1]
703	    # Every left row is visited in left CSV order; each left row expands to
704	    # all of its matching right rows in right CSV order.
705	    for lrow in left_rows:
706	        field = lrow[left_idx] if left_idx < len(lrow) else ""
707	        for rrow in right_buckets.get(_join_key(field), ()):  # inner join
708	            pairs.append((lrow, rrow))
709	
710	    # WHERE runs only after the join has fully expanded the rows.
711	    if query.where is not None:
712	        mask = _eval_join_where(query.where, pairs, where_positions)
713	        pairs = [pair for pair, matched in zip(pairs, mask) if matched]
714	
715	    projected_rows = []
716	    for pair in pairs:
717	        projected_rows.append(
718	            [
719	                _project_value(pair[side][idx] if idx < len(pair[side]) else "")
720	                for side, idx in select_positions
721	            ]
722	        )
723	
724	    result: Dict[str, Any] = {
725	        "columns": [item.text for item in query.select],
726	        "rows": projected_rows,
727	        "row_count": len(projected_rows),
728	    }
729	
730	    # ORDER BY sorts the fully joined/filtered/projected rows; stability
731	    # keeps join row order (left CSV order, then right CSV order). LIMIT
732	    # truncates last.
733	    if query.order_by:
734	        # Resolve each sort item through the two headers (so bare and
735	        # qualified references to the same column are identical) and map it
736	        # to its position in the SELECT list.
737	        order_positions = []
738	        seen: set = set()
739	        for sort_item in query.order_by:
740	            position = resolve(sort_item.table, sort_item.column)
741	            if position in seen:
742	                raise ValueError(
743	                    f"duplicate ORDER BY item {sort_item.text!r}"
744	                )
745	            seen.add(position)
746	            try:
747	                idx = select_positions.index(position)
748	            except ValueError:
749	                raise ValueError(
750	                    f"ORDER BY column {sort_item.text!r} is not in the "
751	                    "SELECT list"
752	                )
753	            order_positions.append((idx, sort_item.descending))
754	        for idx, descending in reversed(order_positions):
755	            result["rows"].sort(
756	                key=lambda row, i=idx: _sort_key(row[i]), reverse=descending
757	            )
758	    if query.limit is not None:
759	        _apply_limit(result, query.limit)
760	    return result
761

763	def _dumps(obj: Any) -> str:
764	    """Deterministic JSON encoder; Decimal values render as decimal numbers."""
765	
766	    def encode(value: Any) -> str:
767	        if value is None:
768	            return "null"
769	        if value is True:
770	            return "true"
771	        if isinstance(value, bool):
772	            return "false"
773	        if isinstance(value, Decimal):
774	            return format(value, "f")
775	        if isinstance(value, int):
776	            return str(value)
777	        if isinstance(value, str):
778	            return _json_string(value)
779	        if isinstance(value, list):
780	            return "[" + ",".join(encode(v) for v in value) + "]"
781	        if isinstance(value, dict):
782	            return (
783	                "{"
784	                + ",".join(
785	                    f"{_json_string(k)}:{encode(v)}" for k, v in value.items()
786	                )
787	                + "}"
788	            )
789	        raise TypeError(f"cannot serialize {type(value).__name__}")
790	
791	    return encode(obj)
792	
793	
794	def _json_string(text: str) -> str:
795	    out = ['"']
796	    for ch in text:
797	        if ch == '"':
798	            out.append('\\"')
799	        elif ch == "\\":
800	            out.append("\\\\")
801	        elif ch == "\n":
802	            out.append("\\n")
803	        elif ch == "\r":
804	            out.append("\\r")
805	        elif ch == "\t":
806	            out.append("\\t")
807	        elif ord(ch) < 0x20:
808	            out.append(f"\\u{ord(ch):04x}")
809	        else:
810	            out.append(ch)
811	    out.append('"')
812	    return "".join(out)
813	
814	
815	def execute(data_dir: str, sql: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
816	    """Run *sql* against CSV tables in *data_dir*; return a result dict.
817	
818	    Raises:
819	        FileNotFoundError: the table's CSV file does not exist.
820	        KeyError: the query references a column absent from the header.
821	        ValueError: the SQL is malformed/unsupported, or a required field
822	            cannot be read as a decimal number.
823	    """
824	    query: Query = parse_sql(sql)
825	    if query.is_join:
826	        return _run_join(data_dir, query)
827	    table_path = Path(data_dir) / f"{query.table}.csv"
828	    # Built-in open raises FileNotFoundError, preserving the required type.
829	    with open(table_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as fh:
830	        reader = csv.reader(fh)
831	        try:
832	            header = next(reader)
833	        except StopIteration:
834	            header = []
835	        for name in query.required_columns():
836	            if name not in header:
837	                raise KeyError(
838	                    f"column {name!r} does not exist in table {query.table!r}"
839	                )
840	        result = _run_batches(reader, query, header)
841	        # ORDER BY sorts the fully computed result rows; LIMIT truncates last.
842	        if query.order_by:
843	            _apply_order_by(result, query.order_by, query.select)
844	        if query.limit is not None:
845	            _apply_limit(result, query.limit)
846	        return result
847	
848	
849	def render(result: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:
850	    """Serialize a query result as a single JSON object."""
851	    return _dumps(result)

1	"""Minimal self-contained SQL lexer and parser.
2	
3	Supported grammar (the complete surface for this baseline)::
4	
5	    query      := SELECT select_list FROM identifier
6	                  [ INNER JOIN identifier ON join_on ]
7	                  [ WHERE boolean ] [ GROUP BY identifier (, identifier)* ]
8	                  [ HAVING having_boolean ]
9	                  [ ORDER BY sort_item (, sort_item)* ] [ LIMIT integer ]
10	    join_on    := identifier . identifier = identifier . identifier
11	    sort_item  := (identifier | count_star | agg_expr) [ ASC | DESC ]
12	    agg_expr   := sum_expr | avg_expr | min_expr | max_expr
13	    select_list:= grouping_column (, grouping_column)*,
14	                  count_star, agg_expr (, agg_expr)*   (grouped aggregate query)
15	                | count_star [, agg_expr ]*            (aggregate query)
16	                | column (, column)*                   (projection query)
17	    boolean    := or_expr
18	    or_expr    := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
19	    and_expr   := factor (AND factor)*
20	    factor     := LPAREN or_expr RPAREN | comparison
21	    comparison := identifier op value
22	    op         := = | != | > | >= | < | <=
23	    value      := number-literal | double-quoted-string-literal
24	
25	HAVING shares the AND/OR/parentheses boolean shape, but its leaves are
26	aggregate-to-number comparisons::
27	
28	    having_boolean := having_or
29	    having_factor  := LPAREN having_or RPAREN | having_comparison
30	    having_comparison := aggregate op number-literal
31	    aggregate      := count_star | agg_expr
32	
33	The left side must be a ``count(*)``, ``sum(column)``, ``avg(column)``,
34	``min(column)`` or ``max(column)`` expression that already appears in the
35	SELECT list; the right side is an unquoted finite decimal literal only (no
36	strings, no columns, no other expressions).
37	
38	A query may name at most one INNER JOIN, in the fixed position directly
39	after the FROM table and before WHERE::
40	
41	    SELECT item, item FROM left INNER JOIN right ON left.a = right.b
42	    [WHERE ...] [ORDER BY ...] [LIMIT n]
43	
44	There are no aliases, no LEFT JOIN, no multiple joins, and a join query is a
45	plain projection only: aggregates/GROUP BY/HAVING are rejected. Column
46	references in the SELECT list, ON and WHERE may be table-qualified
47	(``table.column``); an unqualified column is accepted only when it resolves
48	uniquely across the two tables. ON must be exactly one equality of one column
49	from each table: literals, two columns of the same table, any operator other
50	than ``=`` and combined/duplicate conditions are rejected.
51	
52	AND binds tighter than OR; parentheses may be nested to override the
53	precedence. Parentheses *combine* boolean conditions only: a parenthesized
54	group must itself contain an AND/OR combination (``(a = 1)`` is rejected),
55	and parentheses may never wrap columns, values or comparisons-as-values.
56	There is no NOT, no constant truth value and no other expression forms.
57	
58	HAVING may appear at most once and only after GROUP BY (or after WHERE in
59	an ungrouped aggregate query); it is rejected on plain projection queries.
60	
61	ORDER BY follows HAVING (or WHERE/GROUP BY when HAVING is absent) and LIMIT
62	follows ORDER BY; each may appear at most once and never out of order. Each
63	sort item references a result column already in the SELECT list — a plain or
64	grouping column, ``count(*)`` or one of ``sum(column)``, ``avg(column)``,
65	``min(column)``, ``max(column)`` — with an optional ``ASC`` (default) or
66	``DESC`` direction; duplicate sort items and references to expressions
67	absent from the SELECT list are rejected. LIMIT takes a single non-negative
68	decimal integer literal (digits only: no sign, no fraction, no strings,
69	columns or expressions).
70	
71	A grouped query names one or more distinct grouping columns (at least two
72	for the multi-column shape): they must head the SELECT list in the same
73	order as the GROUP BY list, followed by count(*) and one or more distinct
74	aggregate expressions (``sum``/``avg``/``min``/``max`` over a column).
75	Every aggregate expression — the function name plus its column — may appear
76	at most once in a SELECT list, in grouped and ungrouped queries alike.
77	
78	Anything else (missing FROM, NOT, functions other than
79	count(*)/sum()/avg()/min()/max() in SELECT, wildcards, extra clauses,
80	malformed syntax, unmatched parentheses, OR outside WHERE/HAVING) raises
81	:class:`ValueError`.
82	"""
83	
84	from __future__ import annotations
85	
86	from dataclasses import dataclass
87	from enum import Enum
88	from typing import List, Optional, Tuple, Union
89

91	class _TokKind(Enum):
92	    IDENT = "ident"
93	    KEYWORD = "keyword"
94	    NUMBER = "number"
95	    STRING = "string"
96	    OP = "op"
97	    COMMA = "comma"
98	    DOT = "dot"
99	    STAR = "star"
100	    LPAREN = "lparen"
101	    RPAREN = "rparen"
102	    EOF = "eof"
103	
104	
105	_KEYWORDS = {
106	    "SELECT", "FROM", "WHERE", "AND", "OR", "NOT", "GROUP", "BY", "HAVING",
107	    "ORDER", "LIMIT", "INNER", "JOIN", "ON",
108	}

111	@dataclass
112	class _Token:
113	    kind: _TokKind
114	    text: str
115	
116	
117	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> List[_Token]:
118	    tokens: List[_Token] = []
119	    i, n = 0, len(sql)
120	    while i < n:
121	        c = sql[i]
122	        if c.isspace():
123	            i += 1
124	            continue
125	        if c == ",":
126	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.COMMA, c))
127	            i += 1
128	            continue
129	        if c == ".":
130	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.DOT, c))
131	            i += 1
132	            continue
133	        if c == "(":
134	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.LPAREN, c))
135	            i += 1
136	            continue
137	        if c == ")":
138	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.RPAREN, c))
139	            i += 1
140	            continue
141	        if c == "*":
142	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.STAR, c))
143	            i += 1
144	            continue
145	        if c == '"':
146	            j = i + 1
147	            buf: List[str] = []
148	            while j < n and sql[j] != '"':
149	                buf.append(sql[j])
150	                j += 1
151	            if j >= n:
152	                raise ValueError("unterminated string literal in query")
153	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.STRING, "".join(buf)))
154	            i = j + 1
155	            continue
156	        if c in "=<>":
157	            if i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
158	                tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.OP, c + "="))
159	                i += 2
160	            else:
161	                tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.OP, c))
162	                i += 1
163	            continue
164	        if c == "!":
165	            if i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
166	                tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.OP, "!="))
167	                i += 2
168	                continue
169	            raise ValueError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
170	        if c.isdigit() or (c == "-" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1].isdigit()):
171	            j = i + 1
172	            while j < n and (sql[j].isdigit() or sql[j] == "."):
173	                j += 1
174	            text = sql[i:j]
175	            # Reject malformed numbers such as "1.2.3".
176	            _parse_decimal(text)
177	            tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.NUMBER, text))
178	            i = j
179	            continue
180	        if c.isalpha() or c == "_":
181	            j = i + 1
182	            while j < n and (sql[j].isalnum() or sql[j] == "_"):
183	                j += 1
184	            text = sql[i:j]
185	            upper = text.upper()
186	            kind = _TokKind.KEYWORD if upper in _KEYWORDS else _TokKind.IDENT
187	            tokens.append(_Token(kind, upper if kind is _TokKind.KEYWORD else text))
188	            i = j
189	            continue
190	        raise ValueError(f"unexpected character {c!r} at position {i}")
191	    tokens.append(_Token(_TokKind.EOF, ""))
192	    return tokens
193

195	def _parse_decimal(text: str):
196	    """Validate a decimal numeric literal; return a Decimal-like float-free value."""
197	    from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation
198	
199	    try:
200	        return Decimal(text)
201	    except InvalidOperation:
202	        raise ValueError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}")

205	@dataclass(frozen=True)
206	class ColumnRef:
207	    """A column reference, possibly table-qualified (``table.column``).

318	@dataclass(frozen=True)
319	class Query:
320	    select: Tuple[SelectItem, ...]
321	    table: str
322	    where: Optional[WhereExpr] = None
323	    group_by: Tuple[str, ...] = ()
324	    having: Optional[HavingExpr] = None
325	    order_by: Tuple[SortItem, ...] = ()
326	    limit: Optional[int] = None
327	    join_table: Optional[str] = None
328	    join_on: Optional[JoinOn] = None
329	
330	    @property
331	    def is_aggregate(self) -> bool:
332	        return bool(self.group_by) or self.select[0].kind == "count_star"
333	
334	    @property
335	    def is_grouped(self) -> bool:
336	        return bool(self.group_by)
337	
338	    @property
339	    def is_join(self) -> bool:
340	        return self.join_table is not None
341	
342	    def required_columns(self) -> Tuple[str, ...]:
343	        """Columns the single-table scan must materialize.
344	
345	        Join queries use :meth:`required_join_columns` instead.
346	        """
347	        cols: List[str] = []
348	        seen = set()
349	        for item in self.select:
350	            if item.kind == "column":
351	                if item.column not in seen:
352	                    seen.add(item.column)
353	                    cols.append(item.column)
354	            elif item.kind in _AGG_KINDS and item.column not in seen:
355	                seen.add(item.column)
356	                cols.append(item.column)
357	        if self.where is not None:
358	            self._collect_where_columns(self.where, cols, seen)
359	        return tuple(cols)
360	
361	    @staticmethod
362	    def _collect_where_columns(
363	        node: WhereExpr, cols: List[str], seen: set
364	    ) -> None:
365	        if isinstance(node, Comparison):
366	            if node.column not in seen:
367	                seen.add(node.column)
368	                cols.append(node.column)
369	            return
370	        for operand in node.operands:
371	            Query._collect_where_columns(operand, cols, seen)

374	_OPS = {"=", "!=", ">", ">=", "<", "<="}
375	
376	# Column aggregates over finite decimals, besides count(*).
377	_AGG_KINDS = ("sum", "avg", "min", "max")

380	class _Parser:
381	    def __init__(self, sql: str):
382	        self.tokens = _tokenize(sql)
383	        self.pos = 0
384	
385	    def _peek(self) -> _Token:
386	        return self.tokens[self.pos]
387	
388	    def _next(self) -> _Token:
389	        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
390	        self.pos += 1
391	        return tok
392	
393	    def _expect_keyword(self, word: str) -> None:
394	        tok = self._next()
395	        if tok.kind is not _TokKind.KEYWORD or tok.text != word:
396	            raise ValueError(f"expected {word} but found {tok.text!r}")
397	
398	    def _accept_keyword(self, word: str) -> bool:
399	        tok = self._peek()
400	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.KEYWORD and tok.text == word:
401	            self._next()
402	            return True
403	        return False
404	
405	    def parse(self) -> Query:
406	        self._expect_keyword("SELECT")
407	        items = self._parse_select_list()
408	        self._expect_keyword("FROM")
409	        table_tok = self._next()
410	        if table_tok.kind is not _TokKind.IDENT:
411	            raise ValueError("table name must be a simple identifier")
412	        join_table: Optional[str] = None
413	        join_on: Optional[JoinOn] = None
414	        tok = self._peek()
415	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.KEYWORD and tok.text == "INNER":
416	            join_table, join_on = self._parse_join(table_tok.text)
417	            tok = self._peek()
418	        where: Optional[WhereExpr] = None
419	        having: Optional[HavingExpr] = None
420	        group_by: List[str] = []
421	        order_by: List[SortItem] = []
422	        limit: Optional[int] = None
423	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.KEYWORD and tok.text == "WHERE":
424	            self._next()
425	            where = self._parse_or(join=True if join_table is not None else False)
426	            tok = self._peek()
427	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.KEYWORD and tok.text == "GROUP":
428	            if join_table is not None:
429	                raise ValueError("GROUP BY is not supported in a join query")
430	            self._next()
431	            self._expect_keyword("BY")
432	            group_by = [self._expect(_TokKind.IDENT).text]
433	            while self._peek().kind is _TokKind.COMMA:
434	                self._next()
435	                group_by.append(self._expect(_TokKind.IDENT).text)
436	            self._validate_grouped(items, group_by)
437	            tok = self._peek()
438	        elif join_table is not None:
439	            self._validate_join(items)
440	        else:
441	            self._validate_ungrouped(items)
442	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.KEYWORD and tok.text == "HAVING":
443	            if join_table is not None:
444	                raise ValueError("HAVING is not supported in a join query")
445	            self._next()
446	            having = self._parse_having_or()
447	            if not (bool(group_by) or items[0].kind == "count_star"):
448	                raise ValueError("HAVING is only valid on aggregate queries")
449	            self._validate_having_aggregates(having, items)
450	            tok = self._peek()
451	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.KEYWORD and tok.text == "ORDER":
452	            self._next()
453	            self._expect_keyword("BY")
454	            order_by = [self._parse_sort_item(items, join_table is not None)]
455	            while self._peek().kind is _TokKind.COMMA:
456	                self._next()
457	                order_by.append(self._parse_sort_item(items, join_table is not None))
458	            seen_items = set()
459	            for sort_item in order_by:
460	                key = (sort_item.table, sort_item.kind, sort_item.column)
461	                if key in seen_items:
462	                    raise ValueError(
463	                        f"duplicate ORDER BY item {sort_item.text!r}"
464	                    )
465	                seen_items.add(key)
466	            tok = self._peek()
467	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.KEYWORD and tok.text == "LIMIT":
468	            self._next()
469	            limit = self._parse_limit()
470	            tok = self._peek()
471	        if tok.kind is not _TokKind.EOF:
472	            # Trailing tokens: an unsupported clause, a second ORDER BY or
473	            # LIMIT, a clause out of order, an unmatched ')' or plain
474	            # malformed input.
475	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported or unexpected token {tok.text!r}")
476	        self._validate_qualifiers(
477	            items, where, order_by, table_tok.text, join_table
478	        )
479	        return Query(
480	            tuple(items),
481	            table_tok.text,
482	            where,
483	            tuple(group_by),
484	            having,
485	            tuple(order_by),
486	            limit,
487	            join_table,
488	            join_on,
489	        )
490	
491	    # ----- INNER JOIN -----
492	
493	    def _parse_join(self, left_table: str) -> Tuple[str, JoinOn]:
494	        """Parse ``INNER JOIN right ON left.a = right.b`` after FROM.
495	
496	        Only exactly one INNER JOIN is supported: no aliases, no LEFT/RIGHT
497	        joins, no second JOIN, and ON must be one equality of one column from
498	        each table.
499	        """
500	        self._expect_keyword("INNER")
501	        self._expect_keyword("JOIN")
502	        right_tok = self._next()
503	        if right_tok.kind is not _TokKind.IDENT:
504	            raise ValueError("joined table name must be a simple identifier")
505	        if right_tok.text == left_table:
506	            raise ValueError(
507	                f"join tables must have distinct names: {left_table!r} and "
508	                f"{right_tok.text!r} are the same table"
509	            )
510	        self._expect_keyword("ON")
511	        first_ref = self._parse_column_ref()
512	        op_tok = self._expect(_TokKind.OP)
513	        if op_tok.text != "=":
514	            raise ValueError("ON must be a single column equality using '='")
515	        second_ref = self._parse_column_ref()
516	        tok = self._peek()
517	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.KEYWORD and tok.text in (
518	            "AND", "OR", "INNER", "JOIN", "ON",
519	        ):
520	            raise ValueError(
521	                "ON must be exactly one cross-table column equality, with no "
522	                "combined conditions or further joins"
523	            )
524	        tables = {left_table, right_tok.text}
525	        # Qualified sides are checked here; bare sides are resolved against
526	        # the two headers at execution time.
527	        for ref in (first_ref, second_ref):
528	            if ref.table is not None and ref.table not in tables:
529	                raise ValueError(
530	                    f"ON column {ref.text!r} is not qualified by either "
531	                    "joined table"
532	                )
533	        if (
534	            first_ref.table is not None
535	            and second_ref.table is not None
536	            and first_ref.table == second_ref.table
537	        ):
538	            raise ValueError(
539	                "ON must compare one column from each table, not two columns "
540	                "of the same table"
541	            )
542	        # Bare ON columns are resolved to one side each at execution, once
543	        # the two headers are known; store the sides in written order.
544	        return right_tok.text, JoinOn(first_ref, second_ref)
545	
546	    def _parse_column_ref(self) -> ColumnRef:
547	        """Parse ``identifier`` or ``identifier . identifier``."""
548	        first = self._expect(_TokKind.IDENT)
549	        if self._peek().kind is _TokKind.DOT:
550	            self._next()
551	            second = self._expect(_TokKind.IDENT)
552	            return ColumnRef(second.text, first.text, f"{first.text}.{second.text}")
553	        return ColumnRef(first.text)
554	
555	    def _validate_join(self, items: List[SelectItem]) -> None:
556	        """A join query is a plain projection: no aggregates at all."""
557	        for item in items:
558	            if item.kind != "column":
559	                raise ValueError(
560	                    "aggregate SELECT expressions are not supported in a "
561	                    "join query"
562	                )
563	
564	    def _validate_qualifiers(
565	        self,
566	        items: List[SelectItem],
567	        where: Optional[WhereExpr],
568	        order_by: List[SortItem],
569	        left_table: str,
570	        join_table: Optional[str],
571	    ) -> None:
572	        """Check every ``table.column`` qualifier names a real query table."""
573	
574	        def check(ref_text: str, table: Optional[str]) -> None:
575	            if table is None:
576	                return
577	            if join_table is None:
578	                raise ValueError(
579	                    f"table-qualified column {ref_text!r} is only valid in a "
580	                    "join query"
581	                )
582	            if table not in (left_table, join_table):
583	                raise ValueError(
584	                    f"column {ref_text!r} is qualified by unknown table "
585	                    f"{table!r}"
586	                )
587	
588	        for item in items:
589	            check(item.text, item.table)
590	        for sort_item in order_by:
591	            check(sort_item.text, sort_item.table)
592	        if where is not None:
593	            self._check_where_qualifiers(where, check)
594	
595	    def _check_where_qualifiers(self, node: WhereExpr, check) -> None:
596	        if isinstance(node, Comparison):
597	            if node.table is not None:
598	                check(f"{node.table}.{node.column}", node.table)
599	            return
600	        for operand in node.operands:
601	            self._check_where_qualifiers(operand, check)
602	
603	    def _validate_grouped(
604	        self, items: List[SelectItem], group_by: List[str]
605	    ) -> None:
606	        """Enforce the grouped shape.
607	
608	        SELECT leads with the GROUP BY columns in the same order (distinct),
609	        followed by count(*) and one or more distinct aggregate expressions
610	        (sum/avg/min/max over a non-grouping column).
611	        """
612	        if len(group_by) != len(set(group_by)):
613	            raise ValueError("GROUP BY may not list the same column twice")
614	        if len(items) < len(group_by) + 2:
615	            raise ValueError(
616	                "grouped SELECT must list the grouping columns followed by "
617	                "count(*) and one or more aggregate expressions"
618	            )
619	        for pos, group_col in enumerate(group_by):
620	            item = items[pos]
621	            if item.kind != "column" or item.column != group_col:
622	                raise ValueError(
623	                    "SELECT grouping columns must lead the SELECT list in "
624	                    "the same order as GROUP BY"
625	                )
626	        if items[len(group_by)].kind != "count_star":
627	            raise ValueError(
628	                "grouped SELECT must list count(*) after the grouping columns"
629	            )
630	        seen_aggs = set()
631	        for item in items[len(group_by) + 1 :]:
632	            if item.kind not in _AGG_KINDS:
633	                raise ValueError(
634	                    "grouped SELECT may only contain the grouping columns, "
635	                    "count(*) and sum/avg/min/max aggregates"
636	                )
637	            key = (item.kind, item.column)
638	            if key in seen_aggs:
639	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate aggregate {item.text}")
640	            if item.column in group_by:
641	                raise ValueError(
642	                    f"GROUP BY column {item.column} may not be aggregated"
643	                )
644	            seen_aggs.add(key)
645	
646	    def _parse_select_list(self) -> List[SelectItem]:
647	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
648	        while self._peek().kind is _TokKind.COMMA:
649	            self._next()
650	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
651	        return items
652	
653	    def _validate_ungrouped(self, items: List[SelectItem]) -> None:
654	        """Rules for queries without GROUP BY (the baseline shapes)."""
655	        if items[0].kind in _AGG_KINDS:
656	            raise ValueError(
657	                f"{items[0].kind}(column) requires count(*) in the SELECT list"
658	            )
659	        aggregate = items[0].kind == "count_star"
660	        seen_aggs = set()
661	        for item in items[1:]:
662	            if aggregate:
663	                if item.kind not in _AGG_KINDS:
664	                    raise ValueError(
665	                        "aggregate SELECT may only contain count(*) and "
666	                        "sum/avg/min/max aggregates"
667	                    )
668	                key = (item.kind, item.column)
669	                if key in seen_aggs:
670	                    raise ValueError(f"duplicate aggregate {item.text}")
671	                seen_aggs.add(key)
672	            elif item.kind in _AGG_KINDS:
673	                raise ValueError(
674	                    f"{item.kind}(column) requires count(*) in the SELECT list"
675	                )
676	            elif item.kind != "column":
677	                raise ValueError(
678	                    "count(*)/aggregates cannot be mixed with plain columns"
679	                )
680	
681	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> SelectItem:
682	        tok = self._peek()
683	        # function form: ident '(' ... ')'
684	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.IDENT and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind is _TokKind.LPAREN:
685	            name_tok = self._next()
686	            self._next()  # (
687	            inner = self._next()
688	            self._expect(_TokKind.RPAREN)
689	            upper = name_tok.text.upper()
690	            if upper == "COUNT" and inner.kind is _TokKind.STAR:
691	                return SelectItem("count(*)", "count_star")
692	            if upper in ("SUM", "AVG", "MIN", "MAX") and inner.kind is _TokKind.IDENT:
693	                kind = upper.lower()
694	                return SelectItem(f"{kind}({inner.text})", kind, inner.text)
695	            # Any other function (count(col), median, ...) is unsupported.
696	            raise ValueError(
697	                f"unsupported SELECT expression {name_tok.text}({inner.text})"
698	            )
699	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.STAR:
700	            raise ValueError("wildcard column '*' is not supported")
701	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.IDENT:
702	            ref = self._parse_column_ref()
703	            return SelectItem(ref.text, "column", ref.name, ref.table)
704	        raise ValueError(f"invalid SELECT item {tok.text!r}")
705	
706	    def _expect(self, kind: _TokKind) -> _Token:
707	        tok = self._next()
708	        if tok.kind is not kind:
709	            raise ValueError(f"expected {kind.value} but found {tok.text!r}")
710	        return tok
711	
712	    # ----- WHERE boolean grammar: or_expr := and_expr (OR and_expr)* -----
713	
714	    def _parse_or(self, join: bool = False) -> WhereExpr:
715	        operands = [self._parse_and(join)]
716	        while self._accept_keyword("OR"):
717	            operands.append(self._parse_and(join))
718	        if len(operands) == 1:
719	            return operands[0]
720	        return BoolOp("OR", tuple(operands))
721	
722	    def _parse_and(self, join: bool = False) -> WhereExpr:
723	        operands = [self._parse_factor(join)]
724	        while self._accept_keyword("AND"):
725	            operands.append(self._parse_factor(join))
726	        if len(operands) == 1:
727	            return operands[0]
728	        return BoolOp("AND", tuple(operands))
729	
730	    def _parse_factor(self, join: bool = False) -> WhereExpr:
731	        tok = self._peek()
732	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.LPAREN:
733	            self._next()
734	            node = self._parse_or(join)
735	            self._expect(_TokKind.RPAREN)
736	            if isinstance(node, Comparison):
737	                # Parentheses only *combine* boolean conditions; they may
738	                # not wrap a single comparison, a column or a value.
739	                raise ValueError(
740	                    "parentheses may only group combined AND/OR conditions, "
741	                    "not a single comparison"
742	                )
743	            return node
744	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.IDENT:
745	            return self._parse_comparison(join)
746	        # NOT, dangling AND/OR, ')', EOF, numbers, ...: none can start a
747	        # boolean condition.
748	        raise ValueError(f"expected a boolean condition but found {tok.text!r}")
749	
750	    def _parse_comparison(self, join: bool = False) -> Comparison:
751	        ref = self._parse_column_ref()
752	        if ref.table is not None and not join:
753	            raise ValueError(
754	                f"table-qualified column {ref.text!r} is only valid in a "
755	                "join query"
756	            )
757	        op_tok = self._expect(_TokKind.OP)
758	        if op_tok.text not in _OPS:
759	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported operator {op_tok.text!r}")
760	        val = self._next()
761	        if val.kind is _TokKind.NUMBER:
762	            return Comparison(ref.name, op_tok.text, val.text, False, ref.table)
763	        if val.kind is _TokKind.STRING:
764	            return Comparison(ref.name, op_tok.text, val.text, True, ref.table)
765	        raise ValueError(
766	            "comparison value must be an unquoted number or a double-quoted string"
767	        )
768	
769	    # ----- HAVING boolean grammar: aggregate op number, AND/OR/parens -----
770	
771	    def _parse_having_or(self) -> HavingExpr:
772	        operands = [self._parse_having_and()]
773	        while self._accept_keyword("OR"):
774	            operands.append(self._parse_having_and())
775	        if len(operands) == 1:
776	            return operands[0]
777	        return BoolOp("OR", tuple(operands))
778	
779	    def _parse_having_and(self) -> HavingExpr:
780	        operands = [self._parse_having_factor()]
781	        while self._accept_keyword("AND"):
782	            operands.append(self._parse_having_factor())
783	        if len(operands) == 1:
784	            return operands[0]
785	        return BoolOp("AND", tuple(operands))
786	
787	    def _parse_having_factor(self) -> HavingExpr:
788	        tok = self._peek()
789	        if tok.kind is _TokKind.LPAREN:
790	            self._next()
791	            node = self._parse_having_or()
792	            self._expect(_TokKind.RPAREN)
793	            if isinstance(node, HavingComparison):
794	                # As in WHERE, parentheses only combine conditions; they
795	                # may not wrap a single HAVING comparison.
796	                raise ValueError(
797	                    "parentheses may only group combined AND/OR conditions, "
798	                    "not a single comparison"
799	                )
800	            return node
801	        if (
802	            tok.kind is _TokKind.IDENT
803	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind is _TokKind.LPAREN
804	        ):
805	            return self._parse_having_comparison()
806	        # Plain columns/grouping columns, NOT, numbers, dangling AND/OR,
807	        # ')', EOF, ...: none can start a HAVING aggregate comparison.
808	        raise ValueError(
809	            "HAVING condition must compare count(*) or a "
810	            "sum/avg/min/max aggregate with a number, but found "
811	            f"{tok.text!r}"
812	        )
813	
814	    def _parse_having_comparison(self) -> HavingComparison:
815	        name_tok = self._next()  # the aggregate identifier
816	        self._next()  # LPAREN
817	        inner = self._next()
818	        self._expect(_TokKind.RPAREN)
819	        upper = name_tok.text.upper()
820	        if upper == "COUNT" and inner.kind is _TokKind.STAR:
821	            text, kind, column = "count(*)", "count_star", None
822	        elif upper in ("SUM", "AVG", "MIN", "MAX") and inner.kind is _TokKind.IDENT:
823	            kind = upper.lower()
824	            text, column = f"{kind}({inner.text})", inner.text
825	        else:
826	            raise ValueError(
827	                "HAVING may only compare count(*) or sum/avg/min/max "
828	                "aggregates"
829	            )
830	        op_tok = self._expect(_TokKind.OP)
831	        if op_tok.text not in _OPS:
832	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported operator {op_tok.text!r}")
833	        val = self._next()
834	        if val.kind is not _TokKind.NUMBER:
835	            # Quoted strings, columns, aggregates, keywords, EOF: HAVING
836	            # compares aggregates against finite decimal literals only.
837	            raise ValueError(
838	                "HAVING comparison value must be an unquoted finite decimal number"
839	            )
840	        return HavingComparison(text, kind, op_tok.text, val.text, column)
841	
842	    def _validate_having_aggregates(
843	        self, node: HavingExpr, items: List[SelectItem]
844	    ) -> None:
845	        """Every HAVING aggregate must already appear in the SELECT list."""
846	        if isinstance(node, BoolOp):
847	            for operand in node.operands:
848	                self._validate_having_aggregates(operand, items)
849	            return
850	        for item in items:
851	            if item.kind == node.kind and item.column == node.column:
852	                return
853	        raise ValueError(
854	            f"HAVING aggregate {node.text} is not in the SELECT list"
855	        )
856	
857	    # ----- ORDER BY / LIMIT -----
858	
859	    def _parse_sort_item(self, items: List[SelectItem], join: bool = False) -> SortItem:
860	        tok = self._peek()
861	        if (
862	            tok.kind is _TokKind.IDENT
863	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind is _TokKind.LPAREN
864	        ):
865	            if join:
866	                raise ValueError(
867	                    "ORDER BY aggregates are not supported in a join query"
868	                )
869	            name_tok = self._next()
870	            self._next()  # (
871	            inner = self._next()
872	            self._expect(_TokKind.RPAREN)
873	            upper = name_tok.text.upper()
874	            if upper == "COUNT" and inner.kind is _TokKind.STAR:
875	                text, kind, column, table = "count(*)", "count_star", None, None
876	            elif upper in ("SUM", "AVG", "MIN", "MAX") and inner.kind is _TokKind.IDENT:
877	                kind = upper.lower()
878	                text, column, table = f"{kind}({inner.text})", inner.text, None
879	            else:
880	                raise ValueError(
881	                    "ORDER BY may only reference result columns, count(*) "
882	                    "or sum/avg/min/max aggregates"
883	                )
884	        elif tok.kind is _TokKind.IDENT:
885	            ref = self._parse_column_ref()
886	            if ref.table is not None and not join:
887	                raise ValueError(
888	                    f"table-qualified column {ref.text!r} is only valid in a "
889	                    "join query"
890	                )
891	            text, kind, column, table = ref.text, "column", ref.name, ref.table
892	        else:

894	            # a sort item.
895	            raise ValueError(f"invalid ORDER BY item {tok.text!r}")

907	        if not join:

913	    ) -> None:

915	        for item in items:
